The threat to the environment caused by pollution or by the leakage of oil and gas does not remain restricted to one nation, and its effects are long term. Even when some effects are seen only in particular nations, they reach global proportions because of these long term effects, while some problems are global in nature by themselves. After the wave of globalisation that started in 1990, the interdependence among nations increased, so nations need to act with each other's consent and cooperation to deal with these effects. This is why the Stockholm conference stressed that it is the responsibility of all nations to cooperate to overcome pollution, and why global resources such as oceans, deep seabeds, the atmosphere and outer space are treated as wealth that all nations must look after together.

The concept of human rights has emerged from the concept of natural rights. Natural rights are the rights that we are endowed with because we are born as human beings, and in the same way human rights are those rights that are necessary for living as a human being and as a constituent of society. The American and the French Revolutions proclaimed Liberty, Equality, Fraternity and Justice as human rights. Human rights include the important rights to life, food, clothing, shelter, education and health, and the State has to see to it that these rights are available to everybody. In modern times the concept has broadened, and goals like the protection of the environment and sustainable development are also counted as human rights.

Degradation of the environment means the decline in the quality of the environment that makes it unsafe for living beings. Experts studying the environment believed that industrialisation on a large scale and the increasing need for energy have endangered the environment. Chemical fertilisers and pesticides used in agriculture, sound pollution due to vehicles, radiation from nuclear reactors, and leakages of oil or of chemical gases make the environment unsafe and create various problems. Its visible effects are the extinction of species of plants and animals, decrease in the fertility of soil, water shortage, fluctuation in the proportion of rainfall, global warming, drying up of rivers and lakes, pollution of rivers and seas, incidence of newer diseases, acid rain and thinning of the ozone layer. Because these effects are long term and spread beyond the borders of a single nation, environmental degradation has become an international problem.

Terrorism is spreading fear and terror in a society by using or threatening to use violence against common and innocent people for achieving political goals. It is organised and planned violence. Terrorism is different from traditional war, because a traditional war is a conflict between two or more sovereign States in which the geographical boundaries between nations acquire importance, while terrorist groups can cause violence in any part of the world from anywhere in the world. The aim of a terrorist attack is not to endanger the geographical boundaries, but to challenge a regime in a country or to refuse to acknowledge the existence of the State. So the internal security of a country is threatened along with its external security. Since no nation is capable of countering terrorism entirely on its own, terrorism is considered to be a global problem.

Environmental movements at the national and the international level, with non-governmental organisations taking a bigger role in decision making |

The global wealth of resources such as oceans, deep seabeds, the atmosphere, outer space and genetic resources belongs to all the nations of the world, so it is expected that all nations should look after it.

India has given human rights an important place in its own constitutional and legal system. In the Indian Constitution, human rights have been given the place of Fundamental Rights. Along with the Fundamental Rights, the Constitution gives the government the responsibility of protecting the weaker sections such as women and minorities. In 1993, the Human Rights Protection Act was passed. As per this law, the National Human Rights Commission and the State Human Rights Commissions were established. The Human Rights Commission is responsible for taking cognizance of complaints regarding the violation of human rights and for taking appropriate action regarding such violation.

Terrorism has made a deep and long term impact on international politics, and in the last two decades terrorist conflict appears to have intensified in different countries. Because terrorist groups can cause violence in any part of the world from anywhere in the world, and because their aim is to challenge a regime in a country or to refuse to acknowledge the existence of the State, the internal security of a country is threatened in addition to its external security. Terrorism, along with problems like the struggle against racism and border disputes, is jeopardizing human rights on a large scale, since it spreads fear and terror among common and innocent people.

As remedies, the chapter suggests that the security mechanisms of different nations should work in a concerted manner, because no nation is capable of countering terrorism entirely on its own and it is therefore a global problem. All nations have to come together, cooperate with each other, take concrete action and bring about actual change. If terrorism is completely wiped out and human rights are safeguarded and fostered by all nations, exploitation and violence would reduce and people would be able to achieve their own development safely and securely.
